triage.method: An active concept has at least one parent; orphans are retired. NB an ECL self-reference (<<id) returns the concept whether or not it is active, so it CANNOT be used to test activity.

finding:
The AU-extension hypothesis is NOT supported. Namespace 1000119 dominates the extension concepts found (94 of ~160); Australian namespaces 1000036 and 1000168 account for 39. PrEP was a real AU concept but is not evidence of a pattern.

The material finding is the opposite: an unconstrained search (ecl '*') is UNSAFE. Of 35 exact matches it surfaced, 17 are retired orphan concepts — Septicaemia 154313001, Coronary artery disease 8957000, Genital herpes 154333002 — which look like perfect matches and must never be bound. The <<404684003 constraint was silently protecting against this.

Genuine misses are ~13 and have two causes: wrong hierarchy (Haemodialysis is a procedure, like PrEP) and result truncation (Major depressive disorder ranked 6th against count=5).
recommended_binder_changes: Raise count from 5 to 20; Major depressive disorder was rank 6.
Search <<404684003 OR <<71388002 (procedure), tagging which hierarchy matched.

REQUIRE a parent before binding. An orphan concept is retired; this rule alone would have blocked all 17 bad matches above, and it mirrors the concept-activeness gate this repo already applies to AMT products.
